chunks.arabic_text: مَحْبُوبُ بْنُ حَكِيمٍ. رَوَى عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ تَوْبَةَ "كِتَابَ إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ". وَلَا نَعْرِفُهُ.

translations.en: Mahbub ibn Hakim. He narrated the book "Inna anzalnahu" from 'Umar ibn Tawba. And we do not recognize him.

en.summary: This entry from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* highlights Mahbub ibn Hakim as a transmitter of the specific *Musannaf* titled 'Inna anzalnahu' from the prominent Kufi scholar 'Umar ibn Tawba. The author’s note of 'la na'rifuhu' (we do not know him) suggests that while he may have been a known figure in specific circles, he lacked the widespread recognition required for strong independent authority, marking him as a *majhul* or weak link in the chain of transmission.
en.seo_question: Who is Mahbub ibn Hakim and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.مَحْبُوبُ بْنُ حَكِيمٍ: Mahbub ibn Hakim, the narrator being evaluated
key_terms.عُمَرَ بْنِ تَوْبَةَ: 'Umar ibn Tawba, the source from whom Mahbub narrated
key_terms.كِتَابَ إِنَّا أَنزَلَاهُ: The book 'Inna anzalnahu', a specific work or collection attributed to 'Umar ibn Tawba
key_terms.وَلَا نَعْرِفُهُ: And we do not recognize him, indicating his obscurity or lack of widespread recognition among scholars
